# Partner escalation digest - FIU adapter interop issues

Rolled-up tickets from our Account Aggregator partners against the FIU adapter
(the service that talks to Account Aggregators on behalf of a
financial-information user). The build is clean and the shipped checks pass, so
none of this is caught before deploy. Both reporters emphasise the same
pattern: ordinary traffic is fine, and the failures key off the *content* of
specific values rather than load, timing, or sequence.

---

**AA partner (ticket #4471):**
> Your adapter is rejecting a subset of our callbacks as `invalid` on the
> transaction / consent identifier, and the rejected ids are well-formed UUIDs -
> canonical form, straight from our generator. Most UUIDs go through. We diffed
> accepted vs rejected ids and cannot see what distinguishes them; whatever
> validity check you run is *almost* right, and genuinely malformed ids are
> still (correctly) refused.

**AA partner (ticket #4488):**
> Separately: your outgoing notification timestamps are wrong in the afternoon.
> An event we both logged at 13:47 UTC arrives stamped 01:47 on the same date.
> Date, minutes, seconds all agree; mornings are fine. Our parser now rejects
> some of your afternoon messages outright.

---

**Triage note (ops):** these two are the ones partners have pinned down, but
our own sweep says they are not isolated. A few more of the adapter's small,
deterministic helpers in the same family - identifier and payload handling,
field validation - drift in exactly the same way: correct on the ordinary
values the system produces for itself, wrong by a hair on one specific edge
form that routine traffic never feeds them. Away from those edges everything
behaves, which is why the shipped checks never surface any of it.

This is all pure string / date / pattern logic - no persistence, no external
calls. Restore correct behaviour on these content-dependent edge inputs without
changing anything on the paths that already behave; the project's checks pass
now and must stay passing.

Do not add or modify anything under `src/test/`.

Verify the build with:

    cd /app && mvn -o -q -pl webservice test
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

# 2. Date/time formatting patterns for outgoing notification timestamps

There are exactly **three** literal date-format pattern strings in the entire `src/main` tree:

### 2a. `DateTimeUtil.getISOTimeStamp` — the one used for ALL outgoing timestamps (12-hour `hh` bug)
**File:** `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/finbit/fiuadapter/webservice/utils/DateTimeUtil.java`
**Lines 46-51:**

```java
46:     public static String getISOTimeStamp( Long milliSecond )
47:     {
48:         DateTimeFormatter formatter = DateTimeFormat.forPattern("yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'");
49:         DateTime currentDate = new DateTime(milliSecond, DateTimeZone.UTC);
50:         return currentDate.toString(formatter);
51:     }
```

Exact pattern string (line 48): **`yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'`** — Joda-Time `hh` = **clockhour of halfday (1-12)** with **no AM/PM marker**, so any UTC time from 13:00-23:59 is emitted as 01:00-11:59 (e.g. `2026-08-05T07:30:00.000Z` for 19:30 UTC). The correct ISO pattern is `HH`.

Full file for context (52 lines):
```java
15: public class DateTimeUtil {
26:     public static String getAddedDate( Long currentMilliSecond, int days, int month )
27:     {
28:         DateTime date = new DateTime(currentMilliSecond, DateTimeZone.UTC);
29:         Calendar c = Calendar.getInstance();
30:         c.setTime(date.toDate());
31:         c.add(Calendar.DATE, days);
32:         c.add(Calendar.MONTH, month);
33:         return getISOTimeStamp(new DateTime(c.getTimeInMillis(), DateTimeZone.UTC).getMillis());
34:     }
41:     public static DateTime getcurrentUTCTimeStamp()
42:     {
43:         return new DateTime(DateTimeZone.UTC);
44:     }
```

### 2b. `TimeStampValidation` — inbound parse pattern (5 `y`s, correct `HH`)
**File:** `/app/webservice/src/main/java/com/finbit/fiuadapter/webservice/utils/TimeStampValidation.java`
**Line 23:**
```java
23:             SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'");
24:             sdf.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"));
25:             Date date = sdf.parse(timestamp);
```
Exact pattern: **`yyyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'`** (note **five** `y` characters — lenient parsing masks it, but it is asymmetric with the `getISOTimeStamp` output pattern). Uses 24-hour `HH` here, i.e. the round-trip pair `getISOTimeStamp` (writes `hh`) ↔ `validateTimeStamp` (reads `HH`) is inconsistent.

### 2c. `ECCServiceImpl` — DH key-expiry ISO stamp (correct `HH`)
**File:** `/app/diffie-hellman-services/src/main/java/com/finbit/diffiehellman/service/impl/ECCServiceImpl.java`
**Lines 46-54:**
```java
46:         Date date = new Date();
47:         Calendar cl = Calendar.getInstance();
48:         cl.setTime(date);
49:         cl.add(Calendar.HOUR, dhProperties.getKeyExpiry());
50:         TimeZone tz = TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC");
51:         DateFormat df = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'"); // Quoted "Z" to indicate UTC, no timezone offset
52:         df.setTimeZone(tz);
53:         String expiryAsISO = df.format(cl.getTime());
54:         final DHPublicKey dhPublicKey = new DHPublicKey(expiryAsISO, "", publicKey);
```
Exact pattern: **`yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'`** — this is the *correct* reference form of the pattern that `DateTimeUtil:48` gets wrong.

# 4. `src/test/` directories and test files

**There are NO `src/test` directories and NO test source files anywhere in the repository.**

- Source roots present: `/app/webservice/src/main/java`, `/app/jws-signature/src/main/java`, `/app/kms/src/main/java`, `/app/diffie-hellman-services/src/main/java` (plus `/app/webservice/src/main/resources`).
- `find /app -type d -name "test*" -not -path "*/target/*"` → no results.
- `git ls-files | grep -i test` → no results. Repo history is a single commit (`ff42738 import codebase`), with no deleted test files.
- `.gitignore` lines 4-5 explicitly un-ignore `!**/src/main/**` and `!**/src/test/**`, so tests would be tracked if they existed.

Evidence that tests *used to* exist (build leftovers only, no sources):
- `/app/jws-signature/target/test-classes/com/finbit/fiuadapter/jwssignature/SignatureServiceTest.class` — a single **compiled** test class with no corresponding `.java`.
- `/app/jws-signature/target/generated-test-sources/` and `/app/webservice/target/generated-test-sources/` exist but are empty of files.

Test tooling is already configured, so adding `src/test/java` would work out of the box:
- `/app/webservice/pom.xml`: `junit:junit` (lines 44-49, `scope=test`), `powermock-api-mockito2` (58-63), `powermock-module-junit4` (67-72), `spring-boot-starter-test` (97-102, excludes `junit-vintage-engine`), and profile properties `unit-tests.skip` / `integration-tests.skip` set to `false` for each profile (lines 162-163, 174-175, 186-187, 198-199).
- `/app/jws-signature/pom.xml`: `junit` (48-53), `powermock-api-mockito2` (56-61), `powermock-module-junit4` (65-70).

steps.message:
Fixed five content-dependent defects in the FIU adapter's pure helper family. Build passes (`mvn -o -q -pl webservice test`), no files added or changed under `src/test/`.

## Ticket #4471 — well-formed UUIDs rejected
`constants/GeneralConstants.java:43` — `VALID_PATTERN_UUID` required only **11** hex digits in the final group instead of 12:

```
...-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{11}$   ->   ...-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$
```

Since `Pattern.matches` is a full-string match, a canonical 8-4-4-4-**12** id could never satisfy it. This is the check behind `UUIDGenerator.regaxUUIDvalidation`, used for `txnid`, `consentHandle`, `consentId` and `sessionId` (`ConsentNotificationValidationImpl.java:51,59,64`, `FIDataNotificationValidationImpl.java:67,75`). Verified 5000 generated UUIDs plus canonical vectors now pass, while short/long/non-hex/dash-less/whitespace-padded ids are still refused.

## Ticket #4488 — afternoon timestamps off by 12 hours
`utils/DateTimeUtil.java:48` — the outgoing ISO pattern used Joda's `hh` (clock-hour of half-day, 1-12) with no AM/PM marker:

```
yyyy-MM-dd'T'hh:mm:ss.SSS'Z'   ->   yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'
```

13:47 UTC serialised as `01:47`; mornings coincided so they looked fine. Every outbound notification/response timestamp flows through this one method, and it now round-trips through the inbound parser in `TimeStampValidation.java:23` (which already used `HH`) and matches the correct reference pattern in `ECCServiceImpl.java:51`.

## Additional drift in the same family (ops triage note)

- **`utils/Base64Decoder.java:19`** — decoded JWS payloads with the *standard* Base64 alphabet (`Base64.getDecoder()`) instead of base64url. Payloads are base64url, so decoding threw `IllegalArgumentException` only when the encoded form happened to contain `-` or `_` — purely content-dependent. Its sole caller already decodes the identical string with `getUrlDecoder()` (`ConsentArtifactServiceImpl.java:175`), so the two disagreed. Now `getUrlDecoder()`; verified against a payload containing both `-` and `_`, and plain payloads still decode.
- **`utils/NullEmptyUtils.java:14`** — `isNullorEmpty(String)` tested `val.isEmpty()` rather than `val.trim().isEmpty()`, so whitespace-only values passed as populated through every field/schematic validation. The identical sibling class `jwssignature/util/NullEmptyUtils.java:14` trims; the two have been realigned.
- **`service/consentinit/ConsentInitServiceImpl.java:97`** — `validateCustomerId` is documented to "return the AA ID" from a VUA and is fed to `findByEntityVuaHandle`, but returned the segment *before* the `@` (`split("@")[0]`, e.g. `@9999999999`) rather than the AA handle. Fixed to `[1]`, which is also what the existing `customerIdSplit.size() > 1` guard exists to make safe. Verified `9999999999@onemoney -> @onemoney`, hyphenated handles, padded input, and rejection of `9999999999@` / no-`@` forms.

Left deliberately untouched: `TimeStampValidation`'s `yyyyy` pattern (confirmed byte-identical parse results to `yyyy` for all realistic inputs), `GetDetachedBody.getDetached` (index `[2]` is correct for both detached and full compact serialisations), and the `errorMsg != ""` / `SessionStatus.contains()` quirks, which are consistently replicated across all five `schematicErrorCheck` sites and so are pre-existing behaviour rather than drift.
